exposure: racial and economic residential segregation of home neighborhood
racial and economic residential segregation of hospital neighborhood
cohort: The study included 6461 infants born less than 32 weeks gestational age in New York City between 2010 and 2014.
finding: Infants whose mothers live in neighborhoods with the greatest relative concentration of Black residents had a 1.6 times greater risk of neonatal mortality and morbidity compared to those with the greatest relative concentration of White residents.
